GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2017-01-05T08:19:21Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Why is `new Layer(path...)` used inside `Router` instead of `Layer(path...)`
Description: I'm going through the source code and I've noticed the following. 
In the `router/index.js` the layer is created like this:

```
    var layer = new Layer(path, {
      sensitive: this.caseSensitive,
      strict: false,
      end: false
    }, fn);
```
While, in `router/route` the layer is created like this:

`      var layer = Layer('/', {}, handle);`

Based on the implementation of `Layer`:

```
function Layer(path, options, fn) {
  if (!(this instanceof Layer)) {
    return new Layer(path, options, fn);
  }
```
both calls do the same. Why use different initializations?
